parsed.explanation: Combined regime is a protective state/province inside a hostile national system. National passport/visa rules can refuse entry, strand travellers, or trigger fraud/permanent-ineligibility findings; national and immigration custody is documented as abusive, and national facility rules limit identity-congruent government-funded spaces. Local shield laws, expanded care coverage, and court-ordered prison healthcare materially reduce care and local detention risk. For a minor or guardian, local care protections help, but national school/youth-care hostility and pending ballot initiatives keep exposure elevated. Absence of documented street violence is not safety.

entry_documents.exposure: National rules require birth-sex passport/visa markers; officers can refuse, request evidence, or cite fraud/permanent ineligibility when documents or appearance cast doubt. Reported passport confiscation, blocked processing, citizen detentions, and stranded travellers.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid; courts and legal-aid guides contest or clarify policy; the state/province has no border authority and local institutions are protective.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry mismatch can feed secondary screening, investigation, immigration custody, refusal, and stranding.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National/immigration custody documented: hormone denial, forced-labour programs, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse; national corrections adopted conversion-style practices. In this state/province, birth-sex prison placement occurred as discipline in July 2024.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State/province prisons are court-ordered to provide gender-affirming care and sometimes surgery; listed most protective; shield may reduce care-related confinement severity.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: State/province protections do not cancel national or immigration custody; border or federal detention routes into the harsher national system.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars identity-congruent use of government-funded single-sex spaces; other state/provinces have bans/criminal trespass, with documented arrest and men's-ward detention elsewhere in the parent framework.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state/province is listed most protective and lacks a mapped local facility ban; private/local spaces may be safer, while national court contests continue.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Visitor may avoid local bans but remains exposed in national/funded spaces; ballot changes could alter the local posture.

care_services.exposure: National hostility to youth care, funding freezes, reimbursement threats, provider/teacher criminalization, and school investigations chill care; visitor HRT customs treatment is not documented.
care_services.protection: State/province shield and expanded insurance coverage, plus court-ordered prison care, are documented; shield may block outside actions against care provided locally.
care_services.interaction: Shield helps local care access but does not override entry denial, national funding limits, or immigration/federal custody.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy and domestic-terror reward language label radical pro-transgender ideology as threat; school orders target staff; majority public opinion supports restrictive documents/athletics.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No explicit visitor-facing trans-criminalisation in this state/province; national hate-crime law, some state/province protections, litigation, and injunctions operate.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing raises severity of police/immigration encounters after outing, especially involving advocacy, documents, or schools.

minors_guardians.exposure: For a trans minor/guardian: national school and youth-care hostility, teacher criminalization, reimbursement threats, and possible funding losses; two local ballot initiatives target transgender residents.
minors_guardians.protection: State/province is among most protective; expanded care/shield may protect local care and schooling access, but initiative content and status are unsourced.
minors_guardians.interaction: Families may obtain care locally, yet national entry, funding, and custody rules remain; ballot loss would sharply reduce protection.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented trans-specific violence against foreign visitors or organized sweeps in this state/province; national hostility and partial bias-crime coverage make street safety uncertain.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State/province is listed most protective; local institutions and partial hate-crime/anti-discrimination rules may deter or respond, but traveller incident record is absent.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street risk may be lower than border/national risk, yet absence of evidence should not be read as safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Remedies are patchy: pending court orders, injunctions, litigation, and legal FAQs, while passport/fraud, custody, and ballot outcomes remain unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: State/province courts, shield laws, prison-care rulings, civil-liberties advocacy, and equality maps document avenues; several national orders have been blocked.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Local remedies can reduce care and penalty severity but may not stop entry refusal or national/immigration custody abuse.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.15-A involves routine arrests for presentation, months of abusive pretrial custody, and capital ambiguity. Here border consequences are often refusal/stranding, and this state/province lacks documented visitor-facing facility arrests; severe national custody risk still prevents approaching 0.15.

Similar to 0.35-A border exclusion, but local care shield, most-protective assessment, and no universal accommodation reporting raise the score slightly. Permanent-ineligibility risk and national custody abuse keep it near, not above, this tier.

0.55-B has discretionary secondary screening and administrative denial. This jurisdiction is worse because entry rules can trigger fraud/permanent bars and credible abusive immigration/federal custody, despite local care protections.

0.75-C accepts matching passports, respectful border training, and reliable release. Here birth-sex-only markers, refusal/detention risk, threat framing, and national facility limits put the regime far below 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: National entry, federal/national facilities, and custody dominate the combined regime; local protective rules are real but compartmentalised. An outed adult may find care and confinement protections locally, but can still face border refusal, fraud consequences, or abusive national/immigration custody. A minor/guardian encounters added national school and youth-care hostility, with ballot uncertainty.
